title: Cyrus and the Alibi
premise: Coral Eastwick, the unassuming archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has a private habit of solving the deaths the police file away as accidents. When a nervous stranger pays her in advance to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the killing of cathedral organist Cyrus Vane — she dismisses it as a crank's fantasy until she finds Cyrus's name already written into a centuries-old crypt ledger, dated three days hence. Following a cipher hidden in plain sight among the cathedral's memorial plaques, Coral discovers a conspiracy reaching into the diocese itself, one her anonymous client is entangled in from the wrong side. In the end, Coral must choose between exposing the truth through legal channels that will fail, or letting the intended killer walk free while she engineers justice outside the law — and the client she has grown to trust is revealed as the person who set the whole plot in motion to stop it.
about_author: K. M. Okonkwo is a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing the dead of English cathedrals before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about quiet people who notice what institutions would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the cathedral archive, Coral closes out her third unofficial investigation, filing notes on an 'accidental' fall she proved was murder — and told no one. The beat is quiet competence shadowed by loneliness: justice done, but never acknowledged.

chapters.title: A Client Before the Fact
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A hooded stranger visits the archive at closing time, pays triple her fee in cash, and asks her to prove that organist Cyrus Vane will not be murdered on Sunday. Coral refuses; the stranger leaves a brass key and a name: 'Ask the crypt.' Beat: unease disguised as skepticism.

chapters.title: Locked Crypt, Open Secret
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Using the brass key, Coral enters the sealed crypt and finds fresh candle wax, a folded cassock, and dust disturbed in a pattern too deliberate for vandals. Someone uses the crypt regularly. Beat: the thrill of the hunt reawakening after years dormant.

chapters.title: Cyrus at the Console
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. We meet the organist himself — charming, secretive, rehearsing a requiem no one commissioned. He notices Coral watching him from the triforium and smiles like a man who expected to be watched. Beat: magnetic ambiguity; reader can't tell if he's victim or villain.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than the Lie
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Cross-referencing the crypt ledger against burial records, Coral finds entries added in period-accurate ink for people who never died — including one dated this coming Sunday: C. Vane. Beat: cold dread; the impossible made documentary.

chapters.title: The Dean's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Dean Ambrose Fetterley warns Coral off 'archive fantasies' with impeccable politeness, then asks exactly the wrong question about the ledger. She realizes he knows something. Beat: institutional menace wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: What the Plaques Remember
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Deciphering the cipher hidden in memorial plaque dates and initials, Coral decodes a message: 'THE ORGAN SPEAKS WHERE THE ARCHIVE SILENCES.' The conspiracy is recorded in the building itself. Beat: intellectual exhilaration curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Requiem, Uncommissioned
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus rehearses alone at midnight and confronts a figure in the nave — we hear only his half of the exchange. He agrees to something with visible reluctance. Beat: sympathy deepening; Cyrus is complicit but cornered.

chapters.title: The Client Returns
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her anonymous client makes contact again through a dead-letter drop, revealing only that they are 'inside the chapter house' and terrified. Coral demands a face-to-face meeting; the reply is a single word: 'Sunday.' Beat: trust stretched thin.

chapters.title: Accident Number Four
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A verger who helped Coral with the plaque cipher falls from the bell tower — ruled accidental before dusk. Coral recognizes the staging; it matches her three old cases. Beat: grief and fury; the past cases connect to this one.

chapters.title: Three Old Ghosts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with flashback texture. Coral revisits her three solved-but-buried murders and finds each victim had touched the crypt ledger or the plaques. She has been circling this conspiracy for years without knowing. Beat: vertigo — her private hobby was never private.

chapters.title: The Organ Speaks
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Inside the organ case, Coral finds documents naming a decades-old cover-up: a death in the crypt, falsified records, pensions bought with silence. The ledger isn't predicting murder — it's recording debts. Beat: revelation; motive crystallizes.

chapters.title: Duet in D Minor
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Coral finally corners Cyrus mid-practice; he plays through her questions, then admits he was hired to forge the ledger entry — by someone whose face he'll only reveal in the crypt, Sunday, before the appointed hour. Beat: wary alliance formed.

chapters.title: Police, Politely Useless
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral takes everything to Detective Inspector Halloway, who is sympathetic, constrained, and ultimately unable to act on 'a murder that hasn't happened.' Walking out, Coral spots the dean's car outside the station. Beat: the law fails her; theme lands.

chapters.title: Saturday Vigil
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The night before, Cyrus copies the true ledger, hides it in the organ, and writes a letter he may not survive to send. He thinks about the one person he ever loved and lost to the chapter's silence. Beat: tenderness and fatalism.

chapters.title: Sunday, First Hour
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral hides in the crypt before dawn and witnesses the meeting: the client appears — and so does Dean Fetterley. The client is Fetterley's own sister, Verity, who hired Coral to force the conspiracy into the open before Cyrus could be silenced. Beat: shock reframed as relief.

chapters.title: The Appointed Hour
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The killer — the cathedral's sacristan, keeper of the ledger for thirty years — moves to make the entry true. Cyrus triggers the organ's full voice as a signal; chaos in the crypt; Coral shields Verity as the sacristan flees into the passages. Beat: climax ignites.

chapters.title: Beneath the Nave
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A cat-and-mouse chase through ossuary tunnels. Coral, knowing the crypt's geometry better than anyone alive, turns the killer's own labyrinth against him and traps him at the bricked-in door where the original cover-up began. Beat: triumph earned by knowledge, not force.

chapters.title: Confession in Stone
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The sacristan confesses — the original death, the forged peace, every 'accident' since. But his confession implicates the dean, and the dean controls the evidence chain. Beat: victory hollowed by the scale of rot.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Knowing the diocese will bury the confession, Coral chooses her old method: she doesn't hand everything over. She releases enough to force an independent inquiry while keeping the original ledger as leverage, ensuring the sacristan and dean cannot escape. Beat: moral cost accepted.

chapters.title: The Requiem Actually Sung
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Weeks later, Cyrus performs the requiem properly, for the man who died in the crypt thirty years ago, finally named. Coral sits in the nave, publicly thanked for nothing, privately content. Beat: mourning transmuted into restoration.

chapters.title: Alibi
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, coda. Verity asks why Coral kept the last page of the ledger back. Coral answers that everyone deserves an alibi — even the dead, even herself. She files a new folder labeled with a fourth name: her own. Beat: resonant, ambiguous close.
